analysis:
Examined the two base-text excerpts (lines 31367-33341) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. They hold the unchanged base side of the prompt-contract golden vectors for gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit and gpt-oss-20b. They cover tool-call argument normalisation, tool_choice forcing, unicode and endpoint mapping. The file_changes patch shows head-side edits at other lines. These add additional_context {enable_thinking:false} to some request bodies, change prompt_token_count from 803 to 767, and alter chain_hash values and block boundaries. The same pattern repeats at the ranges near 43739, 44524, 45471, 52354 and 53139. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the head text was not visible. No source code, authorization, attestation, crypto or routing logic changed in the supplied units.

Security-relevant observations, none of which is a finding:
- The vectors are test data only. They are not a trust boundary and carry no secrets. They hold no plaintext consumer data, only synthetic strings.
- The chain_hash and prompt_contract_id values feed the cache-routing and prefix-cache logic (T-041, TB-007). A vector change here indicates that the template or prompt-contract behaviour changed. That behaviour lives in code outside the supplied units: how additional_context.enable_thinking is injected, and whether a client could inject it. An untrusted consumer-supplied request could potentially set additional_context in the request_body, which is a possible cache-key or template-control concern. That would need to be validated in the Swift or Go prompt-canonicalisation code, which was not supplied. Whether it is stripped, allow-listed or provider-injected is unverified.
- The prompt_contract_id is unchanged in the visible hunks while token counts change. The next pass should confirm that the contract id or version is updated consistently with the template change, so that stale cache artifacts are not reused across differing prompts.

No concrete regression can be cited from the supplied evidence. Deeper review of the corresponding code changes is warranted.
